By Zachary Cohen - September 19, 2026 79064 X Facebook Email It’s time for Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season. I strongly suggest you check out the Week 2 NFL Betting Hub , where you’ll find all of the features and picks from my talented co-workers. On top of that, we never stop pumping out good NFL content on our live shows . That’s the beauty of being a subscriber. As a company, we’re relentless in our effort to get you prepared for these games. With that out of the way, let’s get into the fun stuff. Keep reading for my Week 2 NFL best bets and Week 2 NFL player props. MORE: Check out our Pro Picks page for NFL best bets from all of our analysts Philadelphia Eagles at Tennessee Titans – 1:00 pm ET Last week, Barkley rushed for 83 yards on only 15 carries in a win over the Commanders. Now, the star faces a Titans team that allowed 142 yards on 32 carries against the Jets duo of Breece Hall and Braelon Allen. In that game, Tennessee’s Rush EPA/Play Allowed was -0.038, which was right around the -0.043 mark the team posted in 2025. All offseason long, we talked about Robert Saleh shaping up this defense, but there is a chance he won’t be successful in doing so. That said, this might just be a strong matchup for an elite rusher. Barkley is averaging 96.9 rushing yards per game in his last 30 games, and he has rushed for at least 78 yards in five of his last six games. Also, since signing with the Eagles, Barkley is averaging 100.4 rushing yards per game when Philly is favored by between 5.5 and 8 points. I just don’t see any reason he can’t get going in this game, and I’ll throw out the fact that the game script could really favor him. If the Eagles go up early, they’ll begin to rely on the run. Bet: Saquon Barkley Over 75.5 Rushing Yards (-135) & Alt Rushing Yards 100+ (+233 – 0.25 units) Minnesota Vikings at Chicago Bears – 1:00 pm ET I tweeted during last week’s game that I can’t understand how Wentz is the backup over JJ McCarthy, but that’s neither here nor there. Wentz went on to do just fine in a win over the Packers, and I don’t see the Vikings being shy about throwing the ball here. With the Bears having put 59 points on the Panthers, there’s just no way of standing a chance against them without making plays in the passing game. And if Bryce Young can go for 361 passing yards against this defense, you’d think Wentz can reach 225 with all of the weapons he has at his disposal. Also, the absence of Jordan Mason only makes it more likely that Kevin O’Connell will let Wentz cook — even if he’s doing it with a microwave. Wentz only threw for 133 yards in relief of an injured Kyler Murray lat week, but he also threw for at least 236 yards in three of his final four appearances in 2025. Two of those three games featured him throwing for over 300 yards. I’m not sure the result of this game will be pretty for Minnesota, but I see Wentz putting up a pretty decent yardage total. I actually really wanted to get more aggressive with this, but the pricing wasn’t great. Bet: Carson Wentz Over 224.5 Passing Yards (+127) Jacksonville Jaguars at Denver Broncos – 4:05 pm ET Is this a massive overreaction from Week 1? While the Jaguars absolutely pounded the Browns, the Broncos looked lousy in a 31-10 loss against the Chiefs. However, looking back to a year ago, Denver was a better football team than Jacksonville. Also, the Broncos had a better offseason than the Jaguars. So, while things did look ugly offensively last week, I’m chalking it up to a weird game. I don’t think anyone should be sounding the alarms on Davis Webb running the offense, and I feel good about Denver bouncing back at home. Under Sean Payton, the Broncos are 4-1 both straight-up and against the spread in home games with totals of 45.5 or higher. Denver also happens to be 6-1 both SU and ATS after scoring 14 or fewer points in its previous game. Those trends support a much better performance from the Broncos — and especially the Denver offense — in Week 2. It’s also pretty easy to envision the Broncos corners enjoying a matchup with an average group of receivers. Denver can also put some pressure on Trevor Lawrence, and I trust the defense to do well against a shaky Jacksonville backfield. On top of all of that, the Broncos look rather sharp here. While most of the action on our VSiN betting splits pages shows public faith in Jacksonville, the line hasn’t budged. The Eagles should be able to score at least 24 points against the Bears and I just don't see how Chicago is going to find 20+ points with an offense led by a 38-year-old Case Keenum . Keenum is starting for the Bears this week , even though Tyson Bagent cleared concussion protocol and is available to play. I generally trust Ben Johnson to dial up enough trickeration to keep his team in a game where it doesn't have its star quarterback, but this feels like a terrible matchup. The Eagles are a boring boa constrictor, and that's a bad matchup for an undermanned team in prime time. Monday Night Football player props Case Keenum Over 0.5 interceptions (-122, DraftKings) I think the Bears would, in a perfect world, love to keep Keenum's pass attempts down and just run the heck out of the ball if they could, but neither the Commanders nor Titans were particularly effective on the ground against Philly. As such, I think Keenum's going to have to hoist the ball close to 30 times and that should provide an opportunity for the Eagles to jump a route or find a pick. This price is more than reasonable, especially if Keenum and the Bears are chasing points late. Dontayvion Wicks Over 41.5 receiving yards (-110, DraftKings) Wicks' Eagles career has started off in impressive fashion, with the former Packers receiver producing multiple games north of 70 receiving yards, slotting into the starting lineup for Philly and becoming a trustworthy weapon for Jalen Hurts alongside DeVonta Smith . I like him to clear this number against a Bears defense that has been extremely vulnerable to No. 2 receivers so far this season, at least when the weather's cooperated. The Eagles are not going to try and win this game by slinging the ball everywhere and cutting Hurts loose in the red zone. They're gonna want to pound the ball as much as they can and feed Barkley and maybe even Tank Bigsby (who is a decent price at +650). D'Andre Swift (-105, DraftKings) Nothing too fancy for us here, just some good, old-fashioned cheap touchdown scorers. Swift is priced at +100 and should be Keenum's best friend in this spot, given his ability to catch passes out of the backfield. I also considered Colston Loveland here, but I'm a little worried about the tight end rotation for the Bears. Plus, Swift can score rushing or receiving and should get plenty of action in both facets. The Lions’ “Sonic and Knuckles” duo in the backfield was one of the best in the league over the past few years. However, Montgomery was always second fiddle to Jahmyr Gibbs in Detroit. He was always productive, especially in the red zone, but now he has the chance to be the RB1 for the Texans. Over the past three seasons, Montgomery has scored 33 touchdowns on the ground, despite being in that backup role. Now, he should get almost all of the touches when Houston is in the scoring area. The Bills had an awful run defense last season. They ranked 31st in the NFL in defensive EPA/rush and 25th in defensive rushing success rate. This Houston team has struggled with pass protection over the past couple of seasons, so it should try to take advantage of that poor run defense and get the ball to Montgomery whenever possible. Wilson dealt with an injury that kept him out for most of last season, but in the first six games of the season when he was fit, Wilson had at least six catches in four of those six games. This is a good matchup for him to start the season against the Cardinals. Last season, Arizona ranked 22nd in the NFL in defensive EPA/rush and 23rd in defensive rushing success rate. NFL player props are bets on a specific statistical outcome for a specific NFL player. We cover passing yards, rushing yards, receiving yards, and anytime touchdowns in our tool, but there are countless other betting opportunities every week. Every prop bet has two parts: The number (Over or Under 81.5 rushing yards, for example) The price, which determines how much a winning bet returns and reflects the implied probability If two players are lined at 45.5 receiving yards, that does not necessarily mean they have the same implied odds. articles.text: Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions Skip to content Purchase Watch & Listen Login Dashboard Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions By Josh Shepardson | 2026-09-13T09:01:27-04:00 Sep 13, 2026 | View Larger Image NFL Best Prop Bets: Week 1 Picks Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) Sharp Betting Tools: NFL Props: Lines & Odds NFL Spreads, Totals, & Moneylines NFL Weather Forecast & Potential Impact NFL Implied Team Totals NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Watson tore his ACL on January 5, 2025, in Week 18 of the 2024 season. He made his season debut last year on October 26, 2025, in Week 8. Remarkably, Watson didn't skip a beat. In fact, he played the best football of his career. The speedster can get off to a fast start this year, and the Packers might lean into the passing attack more while sorting through their backfield with Josh Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List. The matchup against the Vikings could also prompt them to pass more. Per TruMedia, the Vikings were tied for 12th in expected points added (EPA) allowed per designed rush in 2025 and fifth in yards before contact allowed per rush attempt (1.05). Minnesota's coverage tendencies also boost Watson's receiving outlook. According to the Fantasy Points Data Suite 2.0, the Vikings were first in two-high coverage rate (69.0%) and first in blitz rate (44.7%) in 2025. Watson rattled off a 20% target rate per route and 2.42 yards per route run (Y/RR) on 119 routes against two-high coverage in 2025. Furthermore, he had a 26% target rate per route and 2.47 Y/RR on 77 routes against the blitz last season, reeling in 10 receptions on 20 targets for 190 receiving yards. Watson exceeded 55.5 receiving yards only five times in 11 games in 2025. That said, the Packers have thinned their wide receiving corps, and Watson should exceed last year's 68.6% route participation rate in a less crowded wideout room. On a more expansive route participation rate, with a possible uptick in the Packers' passing rate from last year's 24th ranking in pass rate over expected (-2.1% PROE) out of the gate, Watson should clear 55.5 receiving yards. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Kellen Moore brought his fast-paced brand of offense to the Saints last year. New Orleans played at the NFL's fastest pace in 2025, which is favorable for play volume. The Saints were only 19th in PROE (-0.6%), but their passing tendencies ratcheted up down the stretch. In the final four weeks of the regular season, New Orleans was tied for third in PROE (5.0%). They did play the Titans during those four weeks, and Tennessee's defense faced an NFL-high 6.4% PROE. However, the Saints also played the Panthers, Jets, and Falcons in that period, and they ranked 25th (-1.6%), 21st (-0.3%), and 20th (0.3%), respectively, in PROE faced in the 2025 regular season. The Saints had a banged-up backfield at that point, but Moore's willingness to cut Tyler Shough loose can also be viewed as bullish for his trust in the young quarterback. Speaking of Shough, Johnson excelled with the rookie quarterback. In 10 games that Shough played at least 20 snaps last season, Johnson recorded a 71.3% route participation rate, 16.2% target share, 20% target rate per route, 17.7% air yards share, 8.9-yard average depth of target (aDOT), 4.6 receptions per game, 57.4 receiving yards per game, and 1.97 Y/RR. The pass-catching tight end cleared 41.5 receiving yards in five of his last eight games last year. That includes the final three, when he ripped off 89, 95, and 61 receiving yards. Johnson can pick up where he left off for the Saints, and with New Orleans serving as one of the week's biggest underdogs, he should be in a negative gamescript, necessitating the Saints air it out to keep up with Detroit's high-powered offense. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) I'm not on an island on the Sharp Football Analysis team for this pick. Rich Hribar shouted out Brown over 23.5 receiving yards on the NFL Week 1 Best Bets & Player Props Show . A top-down view is immediately favorable for Brown's receiving outlook. Since 2023, the Bengals are tied for first in PROE (7.9%). Conversely, the Buccaneers have been the NFL's biggest pass funnel since 2023, facing the highest PROE (4.3%). The Bengals don't need their arm twisted to let Joe Burrow cook, but the matchup should also push them in that direction. The matchup is also tasty for Brown. In the 2025 regular season, the Bucs allowed the most receiving yards per game (50.1) and the most yards per target (9.90) to running backs. Brown should also be leaned on as an outlet against Todd Bowles ‘ blitz-heavy tendencies. Tampa Bay had the third-highest blitz rate (35.3%) in 2025, and they've had the second-highest blitz rate (40.8%) since 2023. Meanwhile, among players on the Bengals with at least 40 routes against the blitz since 2024, Brown is tied for second in targets per route run (0.25) and has 30 targets, 23 receptions, 158 receiving yards, and 1.30 Y/RR on 122 routes against the blitz. Finally, in 23 games in which Burrow has played at least 20 snaps since 2024, Brown has tallied a 48.0% route participation rate, 11.3% target share, 0.21 TPRR, 3.7 receptions per game, 23.8 receiving yards per game, and 1.20 Y/RR. Brown should surpass those marks against Tampa Bay's pass-funnel and blitz-heavy defense, putting him over 23.5 receiving yards. Target Opportunity, Not Just Recent Results Recent box scores only tell part of the story. When evaluating NFL player props, focus on the factors that create opportunities. For quarterbacks, that may include pass attempts, rushing volume and expected game script. For running backs, examine carries, targets, snap share and goal-line work. For receivers and tight ends, prioritize routes run, target share and air yards. A player can fall short of his prop and still have an encouraging role. Conversely, a recent hot streak may be difficult to sustain if it came on limited volume or unusually efficient production. The goal is to project what the player will be asked to do in the upcoming matchup, not simply react to his latest performance. 2. Compare Your Projection With the Best Available Line A player prop becomes attractive when your projection differs meaningfully from the sportsbook’s line. Before placing a wager, compare the listed total with statistical projections, expected game conditions and the probability that the player goes over or under. It is also important to compare lines across multiple sportsbooks. One book might list a receiver at 64.5 yards while another offers 62.5. That difference can determine whether the bet wins or loses. If the totals are identical, compare the odds and select the sportsbook offering the better price. Consistently getting the best number can make a significant difference over an entire NFL season. BettingPros’ odds-shopping guide explains why comparing lines is so important. 3. Manage Your Bankroll and Track Every Bet Even well-researched NFL player props will lose because injuries, game scripts, weather and normal performance variance can quickly change an outcome. Establish a dedicated betting bankroll and risk only a small percentage on each wager. BettingPros recommends limiting individual bets to approximately 1% to 5% of your total bankroll. Keep a record of the player, prop, line, odds, stake, result and reasoning behind every bet. Over time, this information can show whether you perform better with certain positions or markets, such as quarterback passing yards, running back rushing attempts or receiver receptions. By Adam Burke - September 19, 2026 43878 X Facebook Email NFL Player Props A lot of the usual suspects had big games in Week 1, but there were others who stood out that got off to better starts than expected. Every week gives us a chance to analyze snap counts, usage rates, targets, carries, and all of the other prop betting options that are available. Dustin Swedelson already gave us some of his favorite player prop bets that lined up with our OptaAI projections. We also have some awesome tools here at VSiN to help with your prop betting picks, including our OptaAI NFL Player Prop Projections , exclusively available to our Pro Subscribers . Whether you use them as confirmation of a play that you already like or scan through to find the biggest edges, it is just another weapon in your arsenal against the sportsbooks while trying to build up that bankroll. I also have my First Touchdown Scorer predictions posted for this week, which includes a tracking spreadsheet of 1st TDs for every team and each individual player. As always, shop around for these Week 2 NFL Player Props. Lines are as of 6:30 p.m. ET on Friday, September 18 and are from DraftKings. Here are my favorite Week 2 NFL Player Prop Bets: Caleb Douglas (MIA) Over 38.5 Receiving Yards (-109) Perhaps last week was a fluke, as Douglas, the rookie wideout from Texas Tech, had five catches for 94 yards, but it’s pretty clear that he’s high up on the pecking order. The Dolphins had 56 offensive snaps and Douglas was out there for 51 of them. Only Malik Washington (55) had more snaps outside of the offensive linemen and QB Malik Willis. So, Douglas is going to be out there with chances. The game state should also help here, as the Dolphins project to trail throughout the game again, and probably by even more than they did last week against the Raiders. Douglas didn’t have any drops on seven targets and caught five passes for 59 yards before contact. With the 49ers probably playing soft zone in the second half, Douglas should have some room to work. Our OptaAI projections have Douglas down for 48.19 receiving yards. Jonathon Brooks (CAR) Under 21.5 Rushing Yards (-108) While the Panthers were busy giving up a million points and a million yards to the Bears, we got a glimpse of how the playing time might go at the running back position. Even with ample opportunities to get Brooks, who missed the entire 2025 season and only had nine carries in 2024, some reps and some time with the starting offense, it didn’t happen. Brooks had just 13 snaps and only four carries. He did have an explosive play in the passing game and maybe that will get him some more playing time in third-down situations, but Chuba Hubbard had a 70% snap share and it’s pretty clear that Dave Canales and Brad Idzik have more trust in the more proven player. That may change as the season goes along, but this looks like Hubbard’s backfield right now. Our OptaAI projections dramatically disagree with 44.11 rushing yards for Brooks this week, so we’ll see if I win or the machines win. Matt Gay (LV) Over 5.5 Kicking Points (-119) Klint Kubiak is a very sharp offensive mind and it’s no secret as to why he got this job. He’s there to help Ashton Jeanty and Fernando Mendoza develop. Unfortunately, he’ll be without Brock Bowers again this week, but the Raiders should be able to put themselves in scoring situations, even against a better team in the Chargers. The Raiders gained 50+ yards on four of their first six drives, including a 93-yard TD drive. But, they slowed down the pace and went into a bit of a shell with the lead over their final five possessions, with three of them going for negative yards. I don’t think Kubiak wanted to show too much in a game that they had in hand. Gay, who was 2-for-2 on FGs and 3-for-3 on PATs, gets to kick inside again here at SoFi Stadium and he’s kicked at a 91.1% success rate in domes in his career, going 51-of-56.
